final: {"number": 806, "label": "question", "route": "answer", "related": [2743, 1488, 1581], "evidence": ["mockito/mockito-core/src/main/java/org/mockito/Mockito.java", "mockito/mockito-core/src/main/java/org/mockito/Spy.java", "mockito/mockito-core/src/main/java/org/mockito/InjectMocks.java", "mockito/mockito-core/src/main/java/org/mockito/ArgumentCaptor.java"], "reply": "Hi, Mockito does not run or pause the Callable. A @Spy wraps your real AsyncExecutorImpl, so the block only runs if that implementation executes it, often on another thread. The test can also finish before that thread reaches your breakpoint, and the debugger may only suspend the test thread. To step through the block deterministically, capture the Callable with ArgumentCaptor (see its Javadoc in org.mockito.ArgumentCaptor): verify the submit call, take getValue(), and call() it from the test thread. You can also set the breakpoint in AsyncExecutorImpl's submit method to confirm the block is reached."}
